The blessed Spirit's office is to act as God's decipherer, by letting His people into the secret of celestial experience, as the key and clew to those sweet mysteries of grace which were before as a garden shut up, or as a fountain sealed, or as a book written in an unknown character.--_Toplady_.

arxiv-2012-09443.title: Trace anomaly contribution to hydrogen atom mass
arxiv-2012-09443.creator: Bao-dong Sun, Ze-hao Sun, Jian Zhou
arxiv-2012-09443.description: Abstract We compute trace anomaly contribution to hydrogen atom mass, which turns out to be related to the part of the Lamb shift. This finding might shed new light on our understandings of the mass structure of QCD bound states, such as, proton.

arxiv-2203-12397.title: On independent domination in direct products
arxiv-2203-12397.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . In [ 13 ] Nowakowski and Rall listed a series of conjectures involving several different graph products. In particular, they conjectured that i ⁡ ( G × H ) ≥ i ⁡ ( G ) ​ i ​ ( H ) i(G\times H)\geq i(G)i(H) where i ⁡ ( G ) i(G) is the independent domination number of G G and G × H G\times H is the direct product of graphs G G and H H .

arxiv-2302-11918.title: Smaller Is Bigger: Rethinking the Embedding Rate of Deep Hiding
arxiv-2302-11918.creator: Han Li, Hangcheng Liu, Shangwei Guo, Mingliang Zhou, Ning Wang, Tao Xiang, Tianwei Zhang
arxiv-2302-11918.description: Abstract Deep hiding, concealing secret information using Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), can significantly increase the embedding rate and improve the efficiency of secret sharing. Existing works mainly force on designing DNNs with higher embedding rates or fancy functionalities. In this paper, we want to answer some fundamental questions: how to increase and what determines the embedding rate of deep hiding.

arxiv-2304-00536.title: Design of a Jumping Control Framework with Heuristic Landing for Bipedal Robots
arxiv-2304-00536.creator: Jingwen Zhang, Junjie Shen, Yeting Liu, Dennis Hong
arxiv-2304-00536.description: Abstract Generating dynamic jumping motions on legged robots remains a challenging control problem as the full flight phase and large landing impact are expected. Compared to quadrupedal robots or other multi-legged robots, bipedal robots place higher requirements for the control strategy given a much smaller footprint. To solve this problem, a novel heuristic landing planner is proposed in this paper.

arxiv-2307-03134.title: Quantum-foundational implications of information erasure upon measurement
arxiv-2307-03134.creator: Alberto Montina, Stefan Wolf
arxiv-2307-03134.description: Abstract A projective measurement cannot decrease the von Neumann entropy if the outcome is ignored. However, under certain sound assumptions and using the quantum violation of Leggett-Garg inequalities, we have previously demonstrated that this property is not inherited by a classical simulation of such a measurement process.

arxiv-2310-07750.title: Cosmological and idealized simulations of dark matter haloes with velocity-dependent, rare and frequent self-interactions 2023 Cosmological and idealized simulations of dark matter haloes with velocity-dependent, rare and frequent self-interactions – G
arxiv-2310-07750.creator: Moritz S. Fischer, Lenard Kasselmann, Marcus Brüggen, Klaus Dolag, Felix Kahlhoefer, Antonio Ragagnin, Andrew Robertson, Kai Schmidt-Hoberg
arxiv-2310-07750.description: Abstract Dark matter self-interactions may have the capability to solve or at least mitigate small-scale problems of the cosmological standard model, Lambda cold dark matter. There are a variety of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models that lead to distinguishable astrophysical predictions and hence varying success in explaining observations.

arxiv-2403-02534.title: Towards Foundation Time Series Model: To Synthesize Or Not To Synthesize?
arxiv-2403-02534.creator: Kseniia Kuvshinova, Olga Tsymboi, Alina Kostromina, Dmitry Simakov, Elizaveta Kovtun
arxiv-2403-02534.description: Abstract The industry is rich in cases when we are required to make forecasting for large amounts of time series at once. However, we might be in a situation where we can not afford to train a separate model for each of them. Such issue in time series modeling remains without due attention.

arxiv-2404-15270.title: Chiral TeraHertz surface plasmonics
arxiv-2404-15270.creator: Ian Aupiais, Romain Grasset, Dmitri Daineka, Javier Briatico, Luca Perfetti, Jean-Paul Hugonin, Jean-Jacques Greffet, Yannis Laplace
arxiv-2404-15270.description: Abstract Chiral engineering of TeraHertz (THz) light fields and the use of the handedness of light in THz light-matter interactions promise many novel opportunities for advanced sensing and control of matter in this frequency range. Unlike previously explored methods, this is achieved here by leveraging the chiral properties of highly confined THz surface plasmon modes.

arxiv-2411-13461.title: Summary of the 16th Applied Antineutrino Physics Workshop 2023
arxiv-2411-13461.creator: Compiled by Liz Kneale, Viacheslav Li
arxiv-2411-13461.description: Abstract Day 1: Overview lectures and neutrino-application reports The 16 th Applied Antineutrino Physics (AAP) Workshop was held in the historic Guildhall in York, UK on September 18–21, 2023. This was the first workshop after the COVID-19 pandemic. The 3-day workshop was followed by a tour at the STFC Boulby Underground Laboratory.

arxiv-2412-07247.title: Driving with InternVL: Oustanding Champion in the Track on Driving with Language of the Autonomous Grand Challenge at CVPR 2024
arxiv-2412-07247.creator: Jiahan Li, Zhiqi Li, Tong Lu
arxiv-2412-07247.description: Abstract This technical report describes the methods we employed for the Driving with Language track of the CVPR 2024 Autonomous Grand Challenge. We utilized a powerful open-source multimodal model, InternVL-1.5, and conducted a full-parameter fine-tuning on the competition dataset, DriveLM-nuScenes.

arxiv-2504-15693.title: A study of two Ramsey numbers involving odd cycles
arxiv-2504-15693.creator: Sayan Gupta
arxiv-2504-15693.description: Abstract . For any two graphs G G and H H , the Ramsey number R ⁡ ( G , H ) R(G,H) is the minimum integer n n such that any graph on n n vertices either contains a copy of G G or its complement contains a copy of H H as a subgraph.

arxiv-2505-19685.title: Graph Guided Diffusion: Unified Guidance for Conditional Graph Generation
arxiv-2505-19685.creator: Victor M. Tenorio, Nicolas Zilberstein, Santiago Segarra, Antonio G. Marques
arxiv-2505-19685.description: Abstract Diffusion models have emerged as powerful generative models for graph generation, yet their use for conditional graph generation remains a fundamental challenge. In particular, guiding diffusion models on graphs under arbitrary reward signals is difficult: gradient-based methods, while powerful, are often unsuitable due to the discrete and combinatorial nature of graphs, and non-differentiable rewards further complicate gradient-based guidance.

arxiv-2508-00909.title: NeuCoReClass AD: Redefining Self-Supervised Time Series Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2508-00909.creator: Aitor Sánchez-Ferrera, Usue Mori, Borja Calvo, Jose A. Lozano
arxiv-2508-00909.description: Abstract Time series anomaly detection plays a critical role in a wide range of real-world applications. Among unsupervised approaches, self-supervised learning has gained traction for modeling normal behavior without the need of labeled data. However, many existing methods rely on a single proxy task, limiting their ability to capture meaningful patterns in normal data.

arxiv-2509-06924.title: Neutron Reflectometry by Gradient Descent
arxiv-2509-06924.creator: Max D. Champneys, Andrew J. Parnell, Philipp Gutfreund, Maximilian W. A. Skoda, J. Patrick A. Fairclough, Timothy J. Rogers, Stephanie L. Burg
arxiv-2509-06924.description: Abstract Neutron reflectometry (NR) is a powerful technique to probe surfaces and interfaces. NR is inherently an indirect measurement technique, access to the physical quantities of interest (layer thickness, scattering length density, roughness), necessitate the solution of an inverse modelling problem, that is inefficient for large amounts of data or complex multiplayer structures (e.g. lithium batteries / electrodes).

arxiv-2602-04566.title: Dual Mind World Model Inspired Network Digital Twin for Access Scheduling
arxiv-2602-04566.creator: Hrishikesh Dutta, Roberto Minerva, and Noel Crespi
arxiv-2602-04566.description: Abstract Emerging networked systems such as industrial IoT and real-time cyber-physical infrastructures demand intelligent scheduling strategies capable of adapting to dynamic traffic, deadlines, and interference constraints. In this work, we present a novel Digital Twin-enabled scheduling framework inspired by Dual Mind World Model (DMWM) architecture, for learning-informed and imagination-driven network control.

arxiv-2602-23280.title: Physics Informed Viscous Value Representations
arxiv-2602-23280.creator: Hrishikesh Viswanath, Juanwu Lu, S. Talha Bukhari, Damon Conover, Ziran Wang, Aniket Bera
arxiv-2602-23280.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Hrishikesh Viswanath, Juanwu Lu, S. Talha Bukhari, Damon Conover, Ziran Wang, Aniket Bera. Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL) learns goal-conditioned policies from static pre-collected datasets. However, accurate value estimation remains a challenge due to the limited coverage of the state-action space. Recent physics-informed approaches have sought to address this by imposing physical and geometric constraints on the value function through regularization defined over first-order partial differential equations (PDEs), such as the Eikonal equation. However, these formulations can often be ill-posed in complex, high-dimensional environments.

pmc-10508907.title: Case report: Fatal traumatic coronary artery dissection—an overlooked complication of chest fracture
pmc-10508907.creator: Tao Jiang, Cheng Qian, Gang Wei, Ling Cheng, Wenwu Zheng, Gong Chen
pmc-10508907.description: Coronary artery dissection caused by trauma is a rare occurrence that can be life-threatening. Accordingly, its rapid identification and treatment are essential to improve patient outcomes. Here, we present a case of a patient who suffered multiple rib and femur fractures after falling from a height of eighteen meters and subsequently experienced persistent chest pain.

pmc-10544363.title: What works in advocating for food advertising policy change across an english region – a realist evaluation
pmc-10544363.creator: Susie Sykes, Megan Watkins, Matthew Bond, Catherine Jenkins, Jane Wills
pmc-10544363.description: BackgroundWith increasing recognition of the role of commercial determinants of health, local areas in England have sought to restrict the advertising of products high in fat, salt and sugar (HFSS) on council-owned spaces, as part of wider strategies to reduce obesity.

pmc-10698165.title: Anchovy boom and bust linked to trophic shifts in larval diet
pmc-10698165.creator: Rasmus Swalethorp, Michael R. Landry, Brice X. Semmens, Mark D. Ohman, Lihini Aluwihare, Dereka Chargualaf, Andrew R. Thompson
pmc-10698165.description: Although massive biomass fluctuations of coastal-pelagic fishes are an iconic example of the impacts of climate variability on marine ecosystems, the mechanisms governing these dynamics are often elusive. We construct a 45-year record of nitrogen stable isotopes measured in larvae of Northern Anchovy (Engraulis mordax) in the California Current Ecosystem to assess patterns in food chain length.

pmc-11507433.title: Sudden Cardiac Death and Channelopathies: What Lies behind the Clinical Significance of Rare Splice-Site Alterations in the Genes Involved?
pmc-11507433.creator: Mauro Pesaresi, Alessia Bernini Di Michele, Filomena Melchionda, Valerio Onofri, Federica Alessandrini, Chiara Turchi
pmc-11507433.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and objectives: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is a natural and unexpected death of cardiac origin that occurs within 1 h from the onset of acute symptoms. The major leading causes of SCD are cardiomyopathies and channelopathies. In this review, we focus on channelopathies, inherited diseases caused by mutations affecting genes encoding membrane ion channels (sodium, potassium or calcium channels) or cellular structures that affect Ca2+ availability.

pmc-11510411.title: Model-Informed Precision Dosing for Personalized Ustekinumab Treatment in Plaque Psoriasis
pmc-11510411.creator: Karine Rodríguez-Fernández, Javier Zarzoso-Foj, Marina Saez-Bello, Almudena Mateu-Puchades, Antonio Martorell-Calatayud, Matilde Merino-Sanjuan, Elena Gras-Colomer, Monica Climente-Martí, Victor Mangas-Sanjuan, Katarina Vučićević, Branislava Miljković
pmc-11510411.description: Background/Objectives: Implementing model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) strategies guided by population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models could enhance the management of inflammatory diseases such as psoriasis. However, the extent of individual experimental data gathered during MIPD significantly influences the uncertainty in estimating individual PK/PD parameters, affecting clinical dose selection decisions.

pmc-11518060.title: Development of a Medical Device Lifecycle Research Database at the MFDS
pmc-11518060.creator: H S Yang, S W Jeon, C H Park, S Y Kim, J H Park
pmc-11518060.description: So-called big data are potentially useful in the healthcare field and are of interest to researchers, industry, and government agencies. Over the past 10 years, Europe, the United States, and Asia have been making efforts to collect and systematically manage information on the entire process from clinical trials to follow-up management of medical devices (MD).

pmc-12409794.title: Inhibition of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling enhances autophagy in HL-60 acute myeloid leukemia cells: An integrative bioinformatic and in vitro study
pmc-12409794.creator: Mohammad Malekan, Armin Dozandeh-Jouybari, Nazanin Joudaki, Mehdi Ahangari, Reza Valadan, Hossein Asgarian-Omran, Saeid Taghiloo
pmc-12409794.description: BackgroundAcute myeloid leukemia (AML) involves uncontrolled proliferation of myeloid progenitor cells and carries a poor prognosis. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway plays a key role in AML pathogenesis by regulating cancer cell proliferation and survival. This study investigates the effects of inhibiting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway on autophagy in AML cell lines, aiming to support targeted therapy development that modulates autophagy.

pmc-12446658.title: Independent predictive role of nutritional markers in kidney function decline and mortality in diabetes
pmc-12446658.creator: Tomohito Gohda, Nozomu Kamei, Marenao Tanaka, Masato Furuhashi, Tatsuya Sato, Mitsunobu Kubota, Michiyoshi Sanuki, Risako Mikami, Koji Mizutani, Yusuke Suzuki, Maki Murakoshi
pmc-12446658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMalnutrition and chronic inflammation are common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and contribute to disease progression and mortality. While the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), geriatric nutritional risk index (GNRI), and controlling nutritional status (CONUT) scores assess nutritional status, their predictive values for CKD progression and mortality in individuals with diabetes, particularly independent of tumor necrosis factor receptor 2 (TNFR2), remains unclear.

pmc-12542558.title: Feasibility and acceptability of safer gambling interventions (social norms and goal setting) delivered via text message for those at low-to-moderate risk of gambling harm: a four-arm randomised controlled feasibility study
pmc-12542558.creator: Emily Arden-Close, Sarah Thomas, Reece Bush-Evans, Abigail Hamson-Ford, Elvira Bolat, Sarah Hodge, Keith Phalp, Ruijie Wang, John McAlaney
pmc-12542558.description: ObjectivesTo assess the feasibility and acceptability of three SMS-delivered safer gambling interventions (goal setting (GS), descriptive norms (DN), injunctive norms (IN)) aimed at reducing the transition from low or moderate risk of gambling harm to problematic gambling, and the feasibility of a full-scale randomised controlled trial evaluating their effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

pmc-12957538.title: Pharmacological and Computational Insights Into the Analgesic, Antipyretic, and Antidiarrheal Potential of Mallotus paniculatus Acetone Extract
pmc-12957538.creator: Md Jahirul Islam Mamun, Md Abdul Alim, Sadia Tamanna Tamim, Md Iqbal Hossen, Sajib Chandro Das, Tanbirul Azim Maharaj, Dipta Debnath, Sajeda Akter, S M Moazzem Hossen, Sultan Zahiruddin
pmc-12957538.description: Mallotus paniculatus (Lam.), a member of the Euphorbiaceae Juss family, is a little tree or shrub that has long been used in folk medicine to cure ailments like fever, wound healing, and postpartum recuperation. In this study, Swiss albino mice were used to evaluate the analgesic, antipyretic, and antidiarrheal properties of the acetone extract of M. paniculatus (AMP).

pmc-13208923.title: A Low-Cycle Fatigue Life Prediction Method for a Drive Shaft Considering the Effects of Loading and Strength Degradation
pmc-13208923.creator: Li Yang, Xingsheng Yu, Feng Liu, Liyong Wang, Jinle Zhang, Ximing Zhang, Jing Zhang
pmc-13208923.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The low-cycle fatigue failure of drive shafts under complex service conditions constitutes a critical issue that undermines the structural integrity and service safety of the transmission system in special vehicles. To improve the prediction accuracy of the low-cycle fatigue life of drive shafts, a low-cycle fatigue life prediction method for the drive shaft that accounts for load effects and strength degradation is proposed.

pmc-13593702.title: Vertical transmission, infection dynamics and risk factors for the occurrence of tick fever agents in beef cattle from a tropical region
pmc-13593702.creator: Lidia Mendes de Aquino, Igor Maciel Lopes de Morais, Vanessa Ferreira Salvador, Luccas Lourenzzo Lima Lins Leal, Warley Vieira de Freitas Paula, Gabriel Cândido dos Santos, Luiz Felipe Monteiro Couto, Dina Maria Beltran Zapa, Luciana Maffini Heller, Marcus Antonio Martins Buso, Evandro Davanco Ferreira de Souza, Felipe da Silva Krawczak

pmc-13639637.title: Preoperative Noble and Underwood Score in Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Stable Prognostic Marker Even among Tumor Marker–Negative Cases
pmc-13639637.creator: Masayuki Urabe, Masaya Hiyoshi, Mami Suzuki, Takahiro Fukai, Yui Hasegawa, Emi Terai, Yoshitaka Kiya, Goki Morizono, Toshiyuki Watanabe, Yojiro Hashiguchi
pmc-13639637.description: Introduction:Reliable and widely applicable tools for survival risk stratification in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain to be established. Although the Noble and Underwood (NUn) score, comprising white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, and serum albumin, has been reported to possess prognostic relevance in some malignancies, its role in CRC has yet to be elucidated.

pmc-13679813.title: Pulmonary dermoid cyst mimicking hydatid cyst: a case report with literature review
pmc-13679813.creator: Fahmi H Kakamad, Harem K Ahmed, Amanj K Hamad, Ari M Abdullah, Ahmed H Ahmed, Rebaz M Ali, Harun Amanj Ahmed, Mohammed Namiq Amin, Mohammed Abdullah Othman
pmc-13679813.description: Intrapulmonary dermoid cyst (mature cystic teratoma) is rare and may mimic common cystic lung diseases, particularly pulmonary hydatid disease. A 26-year-old woman presented with dyspnea and left-sided chest, shoulder, and neck pain. Computed tomography demonstrated a large complex cystic lesion in the left upper lobe with gas locules and associated pleural and pericardial effusions, initially suggesting a hydatid cyst.
